measured.dryrun: bash harness/xc-tenancy/test.sh on 2026-09-03: passed 29, failed 0. conformance PASSED 9/9 against the dry-run adapter with units_checked=13, principals_covered=2, no_principal_admitted=0, cross_tenant_reads=0, cross_tenant_recalls=0, cross_tenant_spend=0; the minimal call is 19 lines of caller code counted by harness/caller_lines.py and names no adapter storage; one call.py run exits 2 and shows a write and an own-tenant read both scoped to tenant-northwind, a spend that decrements only tenant-northwind's own ledger, a read across to tenant-acme refused as cross-tenant-denied (403) with no value disclosed, and a unit with no principal refused at entry as no-principal (422) before any store was touched; a bypass field ('enforce': false) is refused document-invalid (422) before resolve_scope even runs; a spend naming a different target principal is refused cross-tenant-denied rather than silently charged there.
measured.swap: conformance PASSED 9/9 before (dryrun, shared-keyspace-principal-column) and 9/9 after (second, database-per-tenant) against the same 9 cases; sha256 of interface.py+call.py+conformance.py identical across both runs, so the swap was configuration; 3 execution-model axes differ (locus_of_the_tenant_boundary: filtered column vs separate store instance; failure_mode_of_a_wrong_or_missing_principal: returns the wrong rows vs resolves no store; provisioning_cost_of_a_new_principal: a new column value vs a new store instance); ADAPTER=dryrun,second call.py ran the same five-step demo on both bindings and printed scoping_decisions_agree=true at every step - identical scoping decisions from both enforcement points; adapters_run=2 with selected_by=configuration on both report cards.
measured.breakage: the three `!=` principal comparisons removed from adapters/dryrun.py's _read, _recall and _spend, in a copy under out/breakage/, on that one adapter only: conformance exits 1 at 6/9 cases, with cross_tenant_reads 0->1, cross_tenant_recalls 0->5 (a recall now returns the other principal's keys) and cross_tenant_spend 0->1 (a spend now silently charges a different principal's ledger); the untouched second adapter, run from the same out/breakage/ copy, still exits 0 at 9/9 - singling out one adapter, because adapters/second.py's isolation is structural (one store instance per principal) and had no filter in its path to remove.

claimed: live mode until run on the host: adapters/live.py's spend operation has never reached a budget endpoint from here, so TENANCY_BUDGET_URL's key-info response shape (GET {url}/key/info?key=... -> {"info": {"spend", "max_budget"}}) is proposed, not fetched from a live document

adapters/live.py's write, read and recall operations are absent by design, not an unverified stub standing in for a real store: PASS.md A6 records no identity field anywhere in the system (F-a6-05) and no fact names a tenant, so there is nothing tenancy-scoped on this host for TENANCY_STORE_URL to name yet

adapters/second.py is a faithful in-process model of the database-per-tenant execution model (X-xc-tenancy-001), not a binding to a real per-tenant store deployment: its shape, its routing index and its swap procedure are real, no external store is linked in

the operations bind_scope/check_scope/meter_scope xc-tenancy's contract names are marked proposed there because PASS.md states no calls for this concern; this harness's resolve_scope/admit realise that proposed shape, not a recorded call vocabulary

the recall counter and the target_principal spend-impersonation case are this harness's own extension beyond xc-tenancy-implement's ScopeAssignmentRecord/pair-axes shapes, built to exercise cap-memory's recall dimension (X-cap-memory-002) and the budget ceiling's per-principal scoping (F-b4-02) the same way read and write already are

PASS.md records no principal field anywhere and no fact names a tenant (F-a6-05); this harness measures the two enforcement points in isolation, and nothing on the platform's own call path consults either adapter yet
